newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Former Mobutu ally arrested in Kabila's Congo.
newsitem.headline: Former Mobutu ally arrested in Kabila's Congo.

text.p: Laurent Kabila's government has arrested another former associate of ousted dictator Mobutu Sese Seko on suspicion of embezzlement, according to family members.
Businessman Bemba Saolona was arrested on Thursday joining more than 30 dignitaries of the Mobutu regime in detention.
Family members said on Friday that Bemba was taken away from his house by a group of soldiers with an arrest warrant.
"They said he would be held some time for questioning. They have accused him of embezzling public money," his wife said.
"I hope justice will be done, to establish that he is not guilty. Apparently they say he misused funds belonging to the national airline but he was not the boss of Air Zaire."
Kabila came to power in May, ending 32 years of Mobutu rule after a seven-month guerrilla war. Mobutu and some cronies fled into exile before Kabila's forces entered the capital Kinshasa.

Bemba, an affluent businessman, was president of the national business association and a member of the transitional legislature that Kabila has dissolved. He advocated negotiations with Kabila early in the revolt.
Mobutu and cronies reputedly embezzled billions of dollars.

The government has pledged to freeze their foreign bank accounts as part of efforts to return the money to the former Zaire, renamed Democratic Republic of the Congo by Kabila. The government says it has inherited empty state coffers.

Other Mobutu associates arrested include Kithima Bin Ramazani, Mobutu's number two before he introduced bogus democratic reforms in 1990. Houses and cars of ex-dignitaries have been confiscated pending judicial proceedings.
